cards.meaning: not only ... but also (formal connective stacking a second, stronger fact onto the first)
cards.example: 英伟达这次不仅要为OpenAI的巨额资本支出提供担保，而且还要资助他们购买自己的芯片。
cards.examplePinyin: Yīngwěidá zhè cì bùjǐn yào wèi OpenAI de jù'é zīběn zhīchū tígōng dānbǎo, érqiě hái yào zīzhù tāmen gòumǎi zìjǐ de xīnpiàn.
cards.exampleMeaning: This time Nvidia not only has to guarantee OpenAI's massive capex, but also finance their purchase of its own chips.
cards.note: 书面语 / formal, the analyst-note register — heavier than spoken 不但…而且. Unlike 不但…而且 (neutral, works in speech), 不仅…而且 signals the writer is building an argument, often escalating from an already-serious first clause to a more surprising second one. Collocation: 不仅 X，而且 Y, where Y is the sharper or less expected fact.
cards.tiesTo: Nvidia's $600B circular financing with OpenAI — lease guarantee AND chip financing

cards.meaning: to exert pressure (on someone/something); to pressure
cards.example: 参议院正准备立法，向购买俄罗斯石油的国家施压。
cards.examplePinyin: Cānyìyuàn zhèng zhǔnbèi lìfǎ, xiàng gòumǎi Éluósī shíyóu de guójiā shīyā.
cards.exampleMeaning: The Senate is preparing legislation to pressure the countries that buy Russian oil.
cards.note: 书面语 / formal, political and diplomatic register — the word of choice in news coverage of sanctions, trade talks, and central-bank jawboning. Distinguish from 逼迫 (bīpò, 'to force/coerce'), which implies direct coercion leaving no choice; 施压 is pressure applied from outside, the target can still resist. Collocation: 向 + [target] + 施压 ('exert pressure on ___').
cards.tiesTo: The Senate's Russia sanctions bill pressuring China and India as top buyers of Russian oil

cards.meaning: stability; steadfastness — the quality of holding firm under pressure
cards.example: Pinapanatili ng BSP ang katatagan ng piso sa pamamagitan ng maliit na interbensyon, hindi agresibong pagtaas ng interes.
cards.exampleMeaning: The BSP maintains the peso's stability through small intervention, not an aggressive rate hike.
cards.note: Formal/official register — the word central banks and government spokespeople reach for, distinct from 'lakas' (raw strength/power). 'Katatagan' doesn't mean the peso is strong, it means it's being held steady on purpose; you can have katatagan even while weakening slowly, as long as the move is controlled. Root: tatag (firm, resolute).
cards.tiesTo: BSP's light, deliberate intervention to hold the peso steady rather than defend it aggressively

cards.meaning: misleading; causing one to be led astray
cards.example: Sabi ni Gobernador Remolona, nakaliligaw ang numerong iyon dahil sa pangkalahatang lakas ng dolyar, hindi partikular na kahinaan ng piso.
cards.exampleMeaning: Governor Remolona said that number is misleading, because it reflects broad dollar strength, not peso-specific weakness.
cards.note: Formal/media register, from the root 'ligaw' (to stray, to go astray) — sharper and more precise than the informal 'peke' ('fake'), which would imply the number was fabricated. 'Nakaliligaw' means the number is real but points you to the wrong conclusion; it's a word for framing and interpretation, not fraud.
cards.tiesTo: Remolona calling the peso's record-low print a 'misleading number'
